verdicts.summary: Lean has an equivalent formula. The Lean weight is the paper's 𝔞: weight ε n m = (1/20)^n (ε⁻¹)^m m! binom(n+m,m) / ((n+1)^2 (m+1)^2) is 𝔞_{αβ} with ε = ρ, n = α, m = β, and AxisSpace is CoefficientSpace with this weight (AxisCoefficientSpace.lean line 430). The final bound ≤ 80 is stated verbatim by weight_radial_shift_ratio. The middle member of (B.9) — the exact value of the ratio — is not displayed by any one declaration; it is split along weight_eq_core_decay into the core factor and the two square-decay factors. coreWeight_radial_identity gives the core ratio exactly: coreWeight α β / coreWeight (α+1) β = 20(α+1)/(α+β+1), the paper's second and third factors. The remaining factor squareDecay α / squareDecay (α+1) = (α+2)^2/(α+1)^2 is the paper's first factor; the repository states only the inequality form of it, squareDecay_le_four_succ (≤ 4), so recovering the displayed equality needs one line of unfolding squareDecay n = 1/(n+1)^2 and clearing denominators. The bound then combines 20 · 4 · 1 = 80 exactly as the paper does. The Lean statement is for every real ε > 0 and all n, m : ℕ, matching the paper's α, β ≥ 0 and ρ > 0.
